description: 1970: PLAN begins survey operations in Amphritrite Group of Paracel Islands, sets up meterological station on Woody Island (Garver, “China’s push,” 1000-1001).
1971, July: People’s Daily first public assertions of sovereignty over Spratlys since 1958 (Zhang Liangfu, NSQDDSJ, 23).
1971: Building of harbour and wharf on Woody Island in Paracels, forming PLA’s first naval base in disputed area (Garver, “China’s push” 1001).
ongoing_through_notes: 2015, as usage has been continuous since

description: 1973: Advocacy of restrictive position on maritime scientific research in UNCLOS III debates (Samuels, Contest, 118-132).
1973: CAS commences comprehensive surveys of the "Paracel sea area" (SOA, ZGHYNJ 1986, 404).
1974, January: PRC evicts South Vietnam from Paracels by force (USARD, Chinese Amphibious Assaults).
1974 January: PRC occupies Southwestern part of the Paracels.  (USARD, Chinese Amphibious Assaults).
1974: Increased People’s Daily island sovereignty claims.
1974 onwards: construction of military infrastructure in Paracels stepped up (Garver, “China’s push,” 1006).
1975: PLA commences more advanced comprehensive survey of Paracel Islands, using satellite and aerial photography, and sonar and radar mapping. (SOA, ZGHYHNJ 1986, 404).
diminished_notes: No use of force against rivals.

description: 1975, November 25: First claim to Scarborough Shoal in People’s Daily. (Shi Dizu, “Nanhai Zhudao”).
diminished_notes: People’s Daily island sovereignty assertions decrease.

description: 1975, November: Beijing rejects Hanoi’s suggestion of suspending propaganda, publishes Guangming Daily article Paracels and Spratlys have been Chinese territory "since ancient times", and that "all the islands belonging to China will definitely return to the embrace of the motherland" (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 50; Garver, “China’s push,” 1006).
1977, July: first PLAN patrols to the Spratly Islands (Naval Command, "Guanyu 'Nansha Qundao wenti'", 8; Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 58).
1977, October: CAS central SCS comprehensive survey mission. Team lands on Scarborough Shoal (SOA, ZGHYNJ 1986, 404; Zhong Sheng, “China has adequate legal basis”).

1978-1979: Construction in the Paracels intensifies again. After constructing an airstrip on Woody Island in 1978, China starts flights to Hainan. By 1980 they are operating twice-weekly. (Garver, “China’s push.”) On December 26, Hainan-Paracels ferry service officially opens (Nansha, “Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao”).
diminished_notes: No known landing on Scarborough Shoal.

description: 1979: Spike in People’s Daily articles proclaiming sovereignty over disputed island groups.

1979, April: PRC detains 24 Vietnamese military personnel for nearly a year in Paracels after they came within 500 metres of Chinese-held island and allegedly fired on a Chinese patrol boat. (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 67).

1979, December: first PLA marine corps brigade established in Hainan, with responsibility for the SCS, and Guangdong Provincial government also establishes office on Woody Island (Singh, “Continuity,” 1501).
1980, November 8: First PLAN air  excursion to Spratlys, with two bombers patrolling. (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 89).
diminished_notes: No known detentions of VN personnel in Paracels

description: 1980: PRC leaves sovereignty marker on Scarborough Shoal (Duowei, “Feilübin shu ci tiaoxin”).

1980, Sept: PRC Civil Aviation Administration tells international counterparts that from October, airlines would have to avoid a “danger zone” near Hainan. This forced diversions, especially in the high-traffic HK-Bangkok route (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 89) According to Garver there were four danger zones, and the area was between Hainan and the Paracels, “thereby forcing international airlines to negotiate with China as sovereign power” (Garver, “China’s push,” 1007).

1982, Sept 26: Vietnam protests PRC energy exploration contract signed with US companies covering Gulf of Tonkin. Protests again February 12, 1983 (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 93, 95). PRC operations in Yinggehai basin continued to 1988 at least, have probably continued to present.
1982: Harbour constructed on Triton Island, closest of the Paracels to Vietnam (VAFIS, “Sovereignty over the two archipelagos.”).

1983, March 1: SOA East and South Sea Branches send Haijian-41 and Haijian-71 to conduct "patrol surveillance" for first time, on the day the PRC Maritime Environmental Protection Law comes into effect (SOA, “Dashiji: 1983.”).
1983, April 24: PRC State Council announces official names for 287 features, prompting Vietnamese protest at “brutal violation” of its sovereignty (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 97).
1983, May: PLAN supply ship and transport ship conduct first mission to southern Spratly Islands, including exercises at James Shoal (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 97; Garver, "China's push," map).
1984, May-July: first CAS comprehensive survey of Spratly Islands (CAS, Zonghe Diaocha Baogao; Garver, "China's push," map).
diminished_notes: No records of SOA "patrol surveillance"

description: 1984, late: SOA comprehensive survey of central SCS concludes on Jan 7 1985, after 133 days, with 1100 participants, gathering hydrological, meterological, chemical, biological, gravitational, water depth, sonic and water pollution data (SOA, “Dashiji: 1985”).
diminished_notes: No PLA missions to Spratlys

description: 1985, April: SOA South Sea Branch sends 24-person investigation team to Scarborough Shoal, finding no permanent foreign military presence, but temporary air targets and concrete simulated bullets (SOA, “Dashiji: 1985”).
1985, December 31: CCP General Secretary Hu Yaobang, and PLAN commander Liu Huaqing visit Paracels (Fravel, Strong Borders, 292).

1986: Spratly fishing increases (CQCB, “Chuanzhang cheng”). "The central government provided 400,000 RMB to purchase equipment for the five Hainan fishing vessels that spearheaded China’s return to the Spratlys." (Martinson, "Sovereignty fish," 6). This followed State Council “Directive regarding the relaxation of policies, and accelerated development of marine production” (关于放宽政策，加速发展水产业的指示) issued in March 1985, and Department of Agriculture and Fisheries approval of "dive-fishing boats (潜水采捕渔船) from Qionghai, Hainan, to revive production in the Spratlys” (SOA, ZGHYNJ 1994-1996, 45).
diminished_notes: No leadership visits to disputed territories

description: 1987: Spike in People’s Daily articles claiming SCS island sovereignty.

1987, March: PRC persuades UNESCO conference to "request" China establish an oceanic observation station in the Spratly Islands. Fravel writes that this was one of five stations that China agreed to build for a worldwide ocean survey, and that it is unknown whether China manipulated the meeting, but PLA historical works indicate that UNESCO provided an "imperial sword" for establishing the PRC's presence in the Spratlys (Fravel, Strong Borders, 92; Garver, "China's push").

1987, April: PLAN chief admiral Liu Huaqing orders PLAN's first combat patrols in Spratlys (Fravel, Strong Borders, 293). From May 16 to June 6 PLAN conducted its first large-scale patrol of the Spratlys, from Northwest Cay to James Shoal (Garver, “China’s push”). Between April and July the PLAN South Sea Fleet conducted surveys of 600,000 sq km of the SCS (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 113).

1987, April-May: Fourth CAS Spratly comprehensive survey is the largest yet. Authorized by State Council to "strengthen survey research in Spratly waters," the expedition now had two ships, lasted 1.5 months, and had “major significance for correcting charts, exploiting resources and navigation.” (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 114) Sovereignty markers were left at Jackson Atoll, and possibility of occupation was investigated. A Ministry of Geology and Mining survey team also erected an official marker on Louisa Reef (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 120-121).
1987, November: Criticism of Philippines by name marks first time since 1970s that PRC had criticized an ASEAN country by name for SCS activities (Chen, “China’s Spratly policy,” 169).

1988: major spike in People’s Daily articles asserting SCS island sovereignty. On December 15, PRC media make high-profile commemorations of the 42nd anniversary of the “retrieval” (收复) of the Spratlys in 1946, even making mention of the “Taiwan Nationalist Army (台湾国民军队) continuously occupying Taiping Island over the long-term” (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 172-3).
other_possible_cases: 1988, Nov 19: VN protests PLAN guided missile destroyer #134 "suddenly opened fire" twice on a Vietnamese Navy ship #505 on patrol in Spratlys. Nov 24: PRC MFA responds, saying records show the destroyer #134 was at anchor all day. Spokesman Li Jinhua say

description: 1988, January: PRC’s first occupation of Spratly feature, Fiery Cross Reef, followed by five more occupations in March (Liu Huaqing, Huiyilu, 540-541).
1988, March: PRC uses force for first time in the Spratlys, killing 70 Vietnamese sailors at Johnson Reef  (Liu Huaqing, Huiyilu, 540-541).

1988, April 13: NPC establishes Hainan Province, naming the three disputed island groups under its jurisdiction. Vietnam calls it “illegal and invalid,” with FM Nguyen saying China was trying to “legalize” its occupation of the Paracels and complete its “violation” of the Spratlys (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 138-139).

1988, June 11: People’s Daily reports Fiery Cross Reef construction is being accelerated, and that an artificial harbour and reclaimed island have appeared on the reef (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 162). On August 2 construction declared complete, and State Council and CMC issued awards to the constructors (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 164).
1988, August 3: “offensive and defensive” PLA training exercises in Spratlys (Dinmore, “China’s navy on maneouvres”). Similar PLAN exercises were reported in October, 1989.
1989, February 5: Construction begins on harbours on Duncan, Woody, East and Triton Islands (Nansha, “Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao”).
diminished_notes: Fewer RMRB assertions

description: 1989, May-July: Three CAS comprehensive surveys. This was the first time the PRC had made a survey of the northeastern part of the archipelago (including the Reed Bank), and the first time it had “gone deeply into the Danger Area.” (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 178-180, 295). Three comprehensive surveys also in 1990.
diminished_notes: No use of force

description: 1989: PRC begins construction on new airstrip in Paracels. On December 22, Vietnamese state radio quotes a FM spokesman saying China is building an airstrip in the Paracels. "This act of China not only violated Vietnam's sovereignty but also endangered other nations in the region," (Bangkok Post, “Vietnam says China building airbase on Spratlys”). Construction was completed 1991.
1991: increased People’s Daily assertions of SCS island sovereignty
diminished_notes: Only 1 CAS Spratly survey mission

description: 1991, May 21:Chinese combat exercises dispatching small craft in Spratlys (Nansha, “Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao”).
1991, May: PRC fishers from Guangxi state-owned fishing company begin fishing south of 8 degrees latitude in the "Southwest Fishing Groups" (Martinson, "Sovereignty Fish," 2-3).

1992, January 11: PRC sends largest-ever group of 24 Hainan officials and PLA officers, on 12-day inspection of southern Spratlys, where they drop seven sovereignty markers (Yeung, “Group sent to Spratlys”).
diminished_notes: No known PLAN exercises

dyads: CB CM CP CV CU CA
description: 1992, Feb: NPC passes Territorial Sea Law, which names disputed islands, authorizes navy to evict intruders, and demands permission for innocent passage.
diminished_notes: No known CAS Spratly surveys

description: 1992, May 8: China awards 25,000 sq km energy concession (WAB-21) to little-known US oil prospecting company Crestone. Last known activity in WAB-21 was in 1994. (Hayton, South China Sea)

1992: Upgrades of Spratly outposts to third generation of “reef forts” (礁堡). China confirmed arrival of building materials at Gaven Reef on July 9 (Nansha, “Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao”). Vietnam makes official diplomatic protest accusing PRC of violating a November 1991 leaders' agreement (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 225-226).

1992, June: People’s Daily announces first-ever archaeological dig in Spratlys has proved Chinese people’s discovery and use of islands dating back to Qin and Han Dynasties (Jia Yuping, “Nansha chutu”). Politicization of archaeological findings has been fairly continuous since.

1992, Sept: Hainan TV reports PRC survey ship, Hainan-6, is on a drilling mission in the Gulf of Tonkin from September 4 to March 4, and Vietnamese news report says it is in waters 70nm from the Vietnamese coast (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 233).
1993, April 19: Jiang Zemin visits Paracels, along with Defense Minister Chi Haotian and Hainan Provincial Party Secretary (Nansha, “Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao”).
diminished_notes: Fewer People's Daily island sovereignty assertions

description: 1993, March 8: "China has resumed oil exploration activities in disputed waters in the Gulf of Tonkin in a move that could chill Beijing's ties. The mass-circulation daily, quoting Vietnamese Foreign Ministry sources, said Hanoi has confirmed that two Chinese ships began oil-drilling activities in the contested waters about a week ago." (Kyodo via Taffer dataset). In May and September Vietnam protested further Gulf of Tonkin surveys (Nansha, “Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao”).
diminished_notes: No known large-scale official inspections in Spratlys.

description: 1993: Three CAS Spratly surveys, and two more in 1994 (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 298-299).
1994: People’s Daily SCS sovereignty claims spike, and remain elevated in 1995.
diminished_notes: No leadership visits to disputed territories
other_possible_cases: 1994, late July: large PLA exercises on Hainan: "Military analysts described the war game as the most spectacular on the island since the Cultural Revolution." (Inter Press, "China: Military becomes more active in diplomacy")

description: 1994: PRC “built a one-meter-high concrete monument” on Scarborough Shoal (Zhong Sheng, “China has adequate legal basis.”). Destroyed by Philippines authorities in 1997.

1994, April 20-May10: Major PRC fisheries survey. PRC Agruculture Ministry completes 21-day, 3400nm survey of  SCS. MOA official Zhuo Youzhan was quoted as saying the data would be used for ''protection of future development of local marine sources as well as for the supervision of the fishermen in the area' (China to extend fishing rights supervision) It was the first trip to Spratlys by Yuzheng-31. China's "self-designed, self-manufactured, all-weather, unrestricted navigation large-scale fisheries management vessel". (Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ 255) MoA Deputy Minister Wu Jixia, welcoming the ship back, states that "the Party Centre and State Council view with the utmost importance the development of the Spratlys." (Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ 255) The PRC starts paying subsidies for Spratly fishing the same year (Martinson, "Sovereignty Fish," 6).

1994, April 19: Crestone begins seismic survey work in WAB-21; standoff ensues, with two Chinese warships blockading a Vietnamese oil rig in the area (entry #4030, “Dispute narratives – MID 3.0 dataset,” in Ghosn, Palmer, and Bremer, “The MID3 data set.”)

1994, October: Vietnam complains about Chinese fishers “violating” its waters; PRC embassy in Hanoi confirms increased numbers in both Spratlys and Paracels (Torode, “Boats blamed for entering Viet waters.”). In March 1995 the Philippines also protested increases in Chinese fishing in the eastern Spratlys (Kyodo, “Philipine to send 90-100 marines to Spratlys”).
ongoing_through_notes: 2015 (numbers of fishers presumed to have continued at this level at least)

description: 1994, late: China occupies Mischief Reef, establishing a Fisheries Management outpost (Fravel, Strong Borders, 296-298.
1995, May 13: PRC ships block a Philippines Navy vessel headed for Spratlys with journalists on board (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 279-280; also entry #4028 in Ghosn, Palmer and Bremer, “Dispute narratives.”)
diminished_notes: No standoff in WAB-21

description: 1995: PRC places sovereignty markers on Jakcson Atoll and Half Moon Shoal. (PHL Memorial, Annex 67).

1996, June 18: State Council issues Rules on Foreign-Related Marine Scientific Research, which come into effect on October 1, codifying the PRC position on marine scientific research in the EEZ for the first time in domestic regulations.
diminished_notes: People's Daily sovereignty assertions decline
other_possible_cases: 1996, April: PRC threatens economic punishment against Conoco after Vietnam grants it oil exploration rights (Zhang, "Cautious Bully" online appendix).

description: 1996, May 15: PRC announces territorial sea baselines around Paracel Islands, designating a wide expanse of ocean as territorial waters.
diminished_notes: No known coercive on-water behaviour
other_possible_cases: March 5 1996: "A Philippine military official told reporters Friday [1st March] that China has upgraded its structures on a Philippine-claimed reef in the disputed Spratly Islands by mounting electronic equipment on the platforms Maj-Gen Carlos Tanega, ch

description: 1996, April: PRC threats of economic punishment against US companies that signed up in Blocks 133 and 134, . "BEIJING, April 17 -- China said Wednesday a deal between Vietnam and a U.S. company to search for oil and gas in the South China Sea is 'illegal' and an infringement of its territorial sovereignty. 'China has indisputable rights over the Spratly Islands and the adjacent waters,' Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said in a dispatch carried by the official Xinhua news agency. 'Vietnam's approval of foreign companies for oil exploration in the Spratly Islands sea area is illegal and invalid and infringes upon China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests,' Shen said. It was China's second blast in a week at Vietnam for sanctioning the joint venture agreement between Houston-based Conoco and PetroVietnam. With Conoco as project operator, the two companies intend to explore a 1.2 million hectare area (3 million acres) 200 miles off Vietnam in the South Con Son Basin of the Spratly Islands. ...In 1992, China awarded Denver-based Crestone Energy Corp. the right to search for oil and gas off what it calls the Wan An Bei reef of the Spratly Islands, a 2.48 million hectare area (6 million acres) that encompasses all of Conoco's two blocks....China warned Conoco off the project before the contract was signed, according to a report earlier this month in the Houston Chronicle. In a letter to former Conoco chief executive Constantine Nicandros obtained by the newspaper, Chen Bingqian, vice president of the China National Offshore Oil Corp. threatened 'confrontation, losses and liabilities' if the deal was consumated. Conoco's parent company, Dupont, has several joint ventures in China." (UPI, "China raps Vietnam."
1997-1999: Seven CAS Spratly surveys for 9th Five-Year Plan (Anhui, “’Jiu-Wu’ Nansha Qundao”)
other_possible_cases: 1997, mid-year: PRC sends surveillance ships to Scarborough after PHL interferes with ham radio enthusiasts (Zhang, "Cautious Bully" online appendix). This appears to be in response to an unprecedented situation, so it is not clear that PRC would have rea

description: 1997, March 7: Kantan-3 oil exploration rig drills 103km from Vietnamese coast (Balfour, “Analysts puzzled”).
other_possible_cases: 1997: Sabina Reef infrastructures destroyed by PHL - must have been placed there at some point over the preceding years, but date unclear. One photo shows a bamboo hut on stilts on Sabina, possibly in the late 80s or early 90s.

description: 1997, May 7: Philippines protests against PLAN warships approaching two features - Kota (Loaita Island) and Panata (Lankiam). (Richardson, “Is China coveting ‘lost’ lands?”; Abbugao, “China, Philippines exchange diplomatic protests”; entry #4028 in Ghosn, Palmer and Bremer, “Dispute narratives.”).

1997, Oct 21: Ledong agreement signed with Arco. "A cooperation agreement, signed Oct. 21 between Arco and the China National Offshore Oil Co., allows Arco to conduct an initial assessment of the gas potential in the Ledong area, he said. The Ledong gas fields are about 100 kilometers southwest of China's Hainan Island... The Vietnamese foreign ministry on Nov. 22 told the Chinese government that the Arco site 'includes a part which violates Vietnamese territory.'" (Dow Jones via Taffer dataset).
1998: Unprecedented large structures built on Mischief Reef. Philippines on Nov 6 protests presence of "armed ships" there (Taffer dataset).
diminished_notes: No repeat of Kantan-3 incident

description: 1999: number of People’s Daily articles on SCS & sovereignty increases ninefold.
other_possible_cases: 1999, March: PRC fishing ban announced. PHL President Estrada says PHL will ignore the ban IF it covers areas of the PHL EEZ. But unclear if that was the case or not.

description: 2000: MFA Asian Affairs D-G Fu Ying makes very strong private representations to BP management regarding its involvement in Vietnamese offshore oil block 6.1 (Hayton, South China Sea, 136).
diminished_notes: People's Daily sovereignty assertions decline

description: 2000: Ministry of Agriculture increases subsidies for Spratly fishing, including ¥4.2m for Guangxi fishers (GXRB, “Guangxi fishermen receive state subsidies”). There was a 26.2% rise in state-sponsored Spratly fishing boats the same year (SOA, ZGYYNJ 2002, 119).
diminished_notes: No known CAS surveys.

description: 2000, December: US protests interceptions of surveillance jets above SCS (Myers, “Collision with China”).
2001: Repeated harassment of US military aircraft and surveillance ships in SCS EEZ, including EP-3 incident (Vincent, “China and the United Nations Convention,” 10).
diminished_notes: No known repeat of representations to foreign companies involved with Vietnamese oil development.

description: 2001, May: Two Chinese navy vessels, a survey ship, and helicopters sighted at Scarborough Shoal (Gomez, “Philippine military report”). Further PRC increases its activities around Scarborough Shoal occurred in 2002, according to Philippines military report (Kyodo, "China continues").
2002: China reinforces its reef outposts in the Spratly archipelago, according to Philippines military (Kyodo, “China continues”).
diminished_notes: No repeat of EP-3 incident
other_possible_cases: 2002: China introduces Mapping and Surveying Law that specifies that foreign vessels engaged in mapping and surveying in "waters under Chinese jurisdiction" must have prior consent from PRC govt & military.

description: 2002: First mention of enforcement of SCS fishing ban against foreign fishing boats in Fisheries Yearbook (Fisheries, ZGYYNJ 2003, 141).
other_possible_cases: 2002, May & Aug-Sep: CMS shadowing of US and Russian survey work (SOA Yearbook 2003). Location unclear.

description: 2002, June: China held live-fire military exercises in disputed waters near the Paracel Islands, according to Vietnam (Williams, “Don't neglect the Spratlys”). "China's navy conducted routine shooting training southwest of Hainan Island recently. For the safety of the nearby ships, the Chinese side made an announcement in advance," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Liu Jianchao told reporters...In a statement late on Monday, Vietnam's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Phan Thuy Thanh said Hanoi was very concerned about the exercises, some of which, she said, were scheduled to take place in Vietnam's territorial waters." (Reuters via Taffer dataset).

2003, April-June: China sent scientific research ship to the Spratlys, interfered with by Vietnamese ships (NISCSS, “2003 NHDQXSPGBG,” 36). The Philippine government also threatened to file a diplomatic protest with China over its research vessels and warships in the area. (Sorza, “U.S. war games not related to disputed island: Arroyo”).
diminished_notes: No reports of intensified PRC activities around Scarborough Shoal
other_possible_cases: PRC sovereignty markers destroyed by the Philippines in April 2003 - must have been placed there at some point in the preceding years.

description: 2004: Spike in People’s Daily island sovereignty claims.

2004: Expansion of Guangxi fishing in the far southern Spratlys. In 2004 "64 Beihai boats operated in the southern Spratlys. By 2006 that number had increased to 155. These boats caught 14,000 tons of fish worth 77.64m RMB - a 25.7% increase over 2005 and a historical high." (Martinson, "Sovereignty fish," 4).

2004, May and October: PRC Fisheries Administration launches its first two “special operations” against foreign fishing in the Paracels and “Zhongsha Islands.” Law enforcement vessel Yuzheng-46161 was posted permanently to the Paracels (Fisheries, ZGYYNJ 2005, 144). Coercion of Vietnamese fishers in the Paracels has occurred yearly since this time or earlier.
2004, July 6: Ministry of Land and Resources gives PetroChina permission to explore for oil and gas in the southern part of the South China Sea (Reuters, “PetroChina to explore in Spratly chain”).
2004, November: Kantan-3 oil exploration rig drills 63nm from Vietnamese coast (State Department, “Chinese missteps).
2005: Non-regular rights defense patrols begin in Gulf of Tonkin border area and parts of the disputed waters (SOA, ZGHYNJ 2006, 164). Most likely Paracels and central SCS.
diminished_notes: People’s Daily island sovereignty assertions decline.
other_possible_cases: 2005, May-June: PRC survey ship Fengdou-4 and fishing boats increase “operational intensity” near Pratas. (Cable #05TAIPEI2433)

description: 2005, January 8: PRC Maritime Police kill 9 Vietnamese fishers, and wound "many" more. (State Department, “Chinese missteps”).
diminished_notes: No repeat of Kantan-3 incident.

description: 2005: PRC’s NASMG launches crackdown on maps without nine-dash line (Xinhua, “China cracks down on erroneous maps.”).
diminished_notes: No record of further action on PetroChina Spratly concession.

description: 2006: Lobbying campaign against foreign oil companies cooperating with Vietnam begins (Fravel, “China’s strategy,” 303).
diminished_notes: No repeat of fatal Jan 2005 incident
other_possible_cases: “China has constructed sovereignty markers at some basepoints of territorial waters including those in Hoang Sa archipelago of Vietnam" ('Vietnam once again reaffirms its sovereignty…'). Again, timing of when this was done unclear.

description: 2006, June-July: Unilateral oil and gas survey near Paracels with escort that reportedly fended off waves of Vietnamese "armed vessels" (Yang and Peng, "Bihai huige").
2007: Regular rights protection patrols begin, and then expand in scope, in South China Sea (CCTV, Lan Jiang Weishi)
other_possible_cases: 2007, July 3: China creates Sansha city, though it doesn't publicize (Do Thanh Hai & Nguyen Thuy Linh 'China's policy towards'). Plan was shelved until June 2012.

description: 2007: At least two CMS “special operations” against “foreign countries’ rights-infringing activities”, including June-July drilling incident in Paracels, which involved ramming (SOA, ZGHYNJ 2008, 127; CCTV, Lan Jiang Weishi). This was preceded by CMS exercises in May/June 2007 were "the largest air-sea patrol exercise since the founding of CMS" in 1998 (SOA, ZGHYNJ 2008, 19).
other_possible_cases: 2007, April: Possible “expulsion” against a Russian survey ship.

description: 2007: Detentions of Vietnamese fishers increase. In one incident in July, a Vietnamese fishing boat sank and one fisherman was killed, according to Vietnam’s military. This was near Woody Island, according to the Vietnam MOFA (State Department, "Vietnam MFA disputes details of article").

2007: PRC threatens economic interests of foreign oil companies with joint ventures with Vietnam, and in one instance the wellbeing of their staff. "Heavy-handed" MFA protests at short notice over Vietnam’s explorations, threatening Nguyen Phu Trong's visit (State Department, “China-Vietnam: Beijing pressuring Hanoi”). The threats appear to remain in effect through subsequent years.
2008: Regular rights defense patrols increase (CCTV, “Lan jiang weishi”).
diminished_notes: No known fatal incidents with Vietnamese fishers.

description: 2008: Expulsions of Vietnamese fishers in Paracels increase from 100+ in 2007 to 313 in 2008 (Fisheries, ZGYYNJ 2008, 138; Fisheries, ZGYYNJ 2009, 150). Expulsions dropped to 102 in 2009, due to deterrent effect of new policy (NISCSS, “2008-2009 NHXSPGBG,” 49; Fisheries, ZGYYNJ 2010, 124). Expulsion, confiscation of catches and damaging of boats has continued regularly to present.
diminished_notes: No known drilling operations.

description: 2008, September: interference with Vietnamese continental shelf surveys (SOA, ZGHYNJ 2009, 151; State Department, “PRC: cow's tongue claim not licked”). Location unknown, but most likely off VN's central coast as southern part was subject to joint submission with Malaysia.
2009: People’s Daily SCS island sovereignty claims increase.
2009: Regular rights defense patrols increase in SCS (CCTV, “Lan jiang weishi”).
2009: Fishing "convoys" to the Spratlys begin, with increased deployments of FLEC ships (Martinson, "Shepherds").

2009: Detentions of Vietnamese fishing boats in the Paracels peak at 33 for the year, according to Vietnamese sources, having numbered less than 30 across the previous 4 years from 2005 to 2008 (Fravel, “China’s strategy,” 305).

dyads: CB CM CP CV CI CU CA
description: 2009, March: Nine-dash line attached to official diplomatic communication for the first time.
2009, March: Harassment of USNS Impeccable.
2010, April: Regular rights defense patrols increase (CCTV, “Lan jiang weishi”). Sovereignty marker dropped on James Shoal “with important historical significance” (SOA, ZGHYNJ 2011, 148).
diminished_notes: People’s Daily island sovereignty assertions recede.
other_possible_cases: PRC deep-sea submersible Jiaolong plants flag on sea floor in August - not clear if it was in disputed area.

description: 2010: At least 3 major PLA exercises in SCS. Approximately 5-6 were announced each year in 2012, 2014 & 2015, though the PLA's increasing openness may account for some of this higher count. Locations of most are not known, and many were likely in undisputed waters.
diminished_notes: No repeat of Impeccable incident.

description: 2010: Suggestions of “core interest” status for SCS claim.
diminished_notes: Reduced detentions of Vietnamese fishers (Fravel, “China’s strategy,” 305).

description: 2010: FLEC ship forces Indonesian vessel to release Chinese fishers (Currie, “Why is China picking fights with Indonesia?”).

2010, May: PRC sends survey ship M/V Western Spirit with unprecedentedly large fleet of escort ships to conduct seismic surveys near Triton Island (Thuy, “Recent developments,” 11; Martinson “Shepherds,” 199). Vietnam's MOFA spokesperson said that "since late May 2010, China has been sending the M/V Western Spirit seismic survey vessel, together with escort ships, to conduct seismic study in the Tri Ton island area of Hoang Sa archipelago and in the oil and gas exploration lots 141, 142 and 143 on Vietnam's continental shelf, approximately 90 -116 nautical miles from Ly Son island, east of the central province of Quang Ngai." (BBC Monitoring via Taffer dataset).
2011: People’s Daily island sovereignty claims increase.
diminished_notes: No known repeat of PRC-Indonesia standoff.

description: 2011: Regular rights defense patrols increase (CCTV, “Lan jiang weishi”).
diminished_notes: "Core interest" discussion recedes.

description: 2011, Feb 25: PLA missile frigate Dongguan fires 3 warning shots across the bows of PHL fishing boats at  Jackson Atoll. (PHL Memorial, Annex 67).
2011, March: CMS ships confront Philippines survey vessels in Reed Bank. (Chubb, Chinese Nationalism and the Gray Zone)
diminished_notes: No known unilateral energy surveys.

description: 2011, May 24: PRC ships lay markers at Iroquois Reef (Houteng Jiao 鲎藤礁) and Amy Douglas Bank, PHL protests on May 31.
2011, May-June: Two Sino-Vietnamese cable-cutting incidents. (Chubb, Chinese Nationalism and the Gray Zone)
2012: People’s Daily island sovereignty claims spike further.
diminished_notes: Fewer cable-cuttings
other_possible_cases: July, PRC-aligned Cambodia refuses to allow reference to SCS in ASEAN Ministers' Meeting communiqué. Not an assertive action, however, as it didn't really weaken any other state's claim.

description: 2012: Regular rights defense patrols increase (CCTV, “Lan jiang weishi”).
diminished_notes: No Reed Bank confrontations

description: 2012: Seizure and detention of at least 4 Vietnamese fishing boats – 21 Vietnamese fishers and 2 boats detained in March for 49 days, 2 more in May (MOFA, “Viet Nam asks China”; AFP, “Fishermen caught”).
2012, May: Informal economic sanctions on Philippines over Scarborough Shoal standoff. (Zhang, "Cautious Bully"; Chubb, Chinese Nationalism and the Gray Zone)
2012, April onwards: Coercion against Philippine boats at Scarborough Shoal, establishing constant presence.
2012, July: Sansha City established, upgrading administrative status of former Office for Xisha, Nansha and Zhongsha Affairs. (Xinhua, “Guowuyuan pizhun chexiao”).
2012, July: CNOOC offers oil and gas blocks hugging the western side of the nine-dash line, along Vietnam's coast.

2012, August: PRC government ships’ presence in southern South China Sea increases, with CMS boats approaching Malaysian survey vessels (Permal, “The rising turbulence”; Clad and Manning, “Commentary: China's bad diplomacy”). The PRC presence in these areas has increased since this time.

2012, November: Hainan province passes laws authorizing “board and search” of foreign boats in China’s claimed waters (Lim, “Singapore concerned”; Perlez, “Alarm as China issues rules”). New fishing regulations were also passed in late 2013, updating a 2004 version of the same (Thayer, “China’s new fishing regulations”).
2012, May: Passports issued with nine-dash line watermark (Del Callar, "PHL protests China's stamping")

2013: SCS regular rights defense patrols begin to encompass Luconia Shoals (Xinhua, “Maritime official details China’s 2013 patrols”). Malaysia observes seven “intrusions” by 16 Chinese assets in this area during 2013 (Bentley, “Malaysia’s ‘special relationship’ with China”).
diminished_notes: No known cable-cuttings.

description: 2013: PLA exercises in South China Sea increase dramatically to at least 12, before returning to post-2010 average of 5-6 the following year.
diminished_notes: Fewer People’s Daily island sovereignty assertions.

description: 2013, April onwards: PRC patrol boats start maintaining constant presence at Second Thomas Shoal (Quismundo, “Withdraw ships”).
diminished_notes: No known detentions of Vietnamese fishers, and probably fewer incidents in Paracels (see Thayer, "China’s new fishing regulations”).

description: 2013: FLEC ship forces Indonesian vessel to release PRC fishers (Bentley, “Mapping the nine-dash line”; Marshall, “INSIGHT-Remote, gas-rich islands”).

2013: PLAN ship forces USS Cowpens to stop while shadowing Liaoning aircraft carrier in South China Sea. Vessels came within 500m (Li Jing, “United States and Chinese warships nearly collide”). US also complained of “unsafe” aerial passes in 2014.
2013, April: First tourist cruise to Paracel Islands on Coconut Princess. (Global Times, "Islands in the Sun")
2014: People’s Daily island sovereignty claims increase.
diminished_notes: SCS military drills back down to a more normal 5 or so.

description: 2014: PRC uses water cannon and helicopters to drive away Philippines fishermen from Scarborough Shoal. Similar incidents were reported in January and April 2015 (Macatuno, “PH fishers recount ordeal”).
diminished_notes: No known coercive fisheries incidents involving Indonesia.

description: 2014: large-scale land reclamation creating artificial islands in Spratlys, including airstrips. (AMTI, "Island Tracker").
2014, March: PRC blocks supply ships on way to Second Thomas Shoal (Reuters, “China says expels”).

2014: May-July: HYSY-981 oil rig incident: PRC sends unprecedentedly large rig with unprecedentedly large escort fleet operating on instructions to coerce to implement survey southwest of Triton Island. (Long, China's Decision to Deploy HYSY-981; Chubb, Chinese Nationalism and the Gray Zone, pp. 71-75)
2014, June: two PRC hydrographic ships operate in Reed Bank, Philippines protests (AP, “Philippine leader questions intent”).
2014: PRC begins maintaining permanent presence at Luconia Shoals (Yang et al., “Weilan de mingji”; Bernama, “China’s presence”).

2015: PRC radio voiceovers challenge US, Philippine and Australian aircraft, demanding they leave airspace near Spratly artificial islands (Tiezzi, “'Nearly all' Australian patrols in South China Sea are challenged”). This practice may have begun earlier.
diminished_notes: No repeat of Second Thomas Shoal supply ship incident.
other_possible_cases: 2015: Vietnam alleges obstruction of at least four rescue missions in Paracels  ("Chinese boats tried to sabotage Vietnam’s rescue mission") But these may have been the result of change in Vietnamese policy (ie. trying to rescue fishers from PRC harassmen

description: 2015: Malaysian fishers “chased” from Luconia Shoals by Chinese ships (Borneo Post, “Chinese Navy bar local fishermen from Luconia shoals”).
diminished_notes: No repeat of HYSY-981 incident.

description: 2015, July-Nov: three coercive actions against Vietnamese ships around Spratly Islands (Tuoi Tre, “Chinese warship soldiers point guns.”)
diminished_notes: US reports reduction in “unsafe” incidents (DOD, Asia-Pacific Maritime Security Strategy, 14).

description: 2015: PRC's Spratly island building intensifies further (AMTI, "Island Tracker").
diminished_notes: No reports of surveys in Reed Bank.

description: 1970, August: Philippines occupies Nanshan Island, and possibly Flat Island. Most accounts say August, but July and September are also mentioned (NSQDDSJ 17-18, 118, 205, 233, 237; Hayton, The South China Sea, 102; AMTI, "Island Features"). Northeast Cay (Parola) and Southwest Cay may both already be occupied.
other_possible_cases: 1970: Oil exploration begins off the coast of Palawan. (Hayton, The South China Sea, 69) Needs verification

description: 1970: Exploration of Reed Bank begins (PXP, "SC 72 Recto Bank"; Hayton, The South China Sea, 69).
1971, April-May: Philippines occupies Thitu (aka Pagasa, aka Zhongye) Island. (NSZGSZHS 118, 233-234, 237
other_possible_cases: 1971: Philippines creates Western Command. Hayton says 1971, Chinese source says 1976. (Hayton, The South China Sea, 69; NSQDDSJ 65)

description: 1971 July: Philippine forces tried to land on Itu Aba but are repelled by Taiwanese forces. (Hayton, The South China Sea, 69; NSZGSZHS 234; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 19; FEER Dec 31 1973, 'Formidable task for Peking' p.39)
other_possible_cases: 1971 (or 1970): Hayton also claims that the Philippines North Danger Reef. Have not seen this elsewhere, but Philippines definately looses Southwest Cay, which is part of North Danger (?), to Vietnam in 1975... (Hayton, The South China Sea, 102)

description: 1971 July: Diplomatic protests and statements from Philippine government over Taiwanese presence on Itu Aba. (NSZGSZHS 234; NSQDDSJ 19, 21)

1971 July 11: President Marcos says the Spratly Islands are disputed, that the Philippines has occupied Nanshan, Flat, and Thitu Islands, and has started oil exploration [or has the right to conduct]. Also claims that the islands belong to no one and that occupation equals control. (NSZGSZHS 15-16, 118, 234-236; Hayton, The South China Sea, 69).

1971 July: Philippines occupies Loaita Island (July 14), Northeast Cay (July 30), and West York Island (July 10 or 30). (NSQDDSJ 17-18; NSZGSZHS 118, 236-237). Total under occupation now appears to be 7, assuming Southwest Cay was already being occupied.

1972, April: Kalayaan Islands officially designated as part of Palawan Province. (Marlay, "China, the Philippines, and the Spratly Islands", p. 203; Dolven, Manyin, and Kan, "Maritime Territorial Disputes in Asia," 14; Ji Guoxing, "Maritime Jurisdiction," note 43).

1972 December: The Philippine-Texaco Oil Company, Philippine-California Mobil Oil Company, and several Philippine companies enter into a partnership to conduct exploration west of Palawan island. Previously, the Philippine government had awarded a Philippine-American resource company a lease at Reed Bank. (NSQDDSJ 23-24)
1973 May 25: Philippines government and an American oil company, Wendell Phillips Oil Co., sign an oil exploration and development contract for west of Palawan.  (NSQDDSJ 24)
1973 June: A "research group" for a Philippine fishing company conducts surveys in the Spratlys, visiting Philippine-occupied islands (NSZGSZHS 236).

1973, December (approx): Seismic surveys start on Wendell Phillips offshore prospect, six months after signing of the agreement. (NSQDDSJ 24). By 1976, Philippine companies were also working with foreign companies (Swedish, Canadian, American,  etc.) to conduct seismic surveys in the Spratlys, including at Amboyna (Anbo) Cay. (NSQDDSJ 50-55; NSZGSZHS 35; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 20) Elsewhere, Chinese sources say this was 1975 (NSQDDSJ 105-106).

1974 February: Philippines protests South Vietnam and Taiwan's claims in the Spratlys via diplomatic notes, welcomes participation form the UN or Allies in solving the dispute,  reiterates that Philippines-claimed islands are not part of the Spratlys, and emphasizes res nullius. The same note(s) then submitted to the UN. (NSQDDSJ 35-36; 40-41; NSZGSZHS  119-120, 238-243)
other_possible_cases: 1974 February:  According to a Vietnamese military official, the Philippines military has occupied an additional two islands in the Spratly Islands, but Philippines denies, saying it sent technical personnel but no new troops (NSZGSZHS 241). Chen Jie says

description: 1974: Philippine government forces Tomas Cloma to sell Freedomland to the Philippine government for one peso. (Hayton, The South China Sea, 70).
other_possible_cases: 1974: Philippines authorizes a consortium of companies to explore for oil in the Reed Bank. (Kivimaki 56) However, according to a Chinese source, the Philippine government had already awarded a Philippine-American resource company a lease at Reed Bank. (N

description: 1976 January: Philippines National Oil (菲律宾国家石油局) and Swedish "Salan Group" (萨兰集团) sign a joint service contract, permitting some foreign (including Swedish and American) and Philippine companies to form the "Reed Bank Consortium" (礼乐滩财团) to conduct exploration at Reed Bank.  Another source says Amoco International was involved (Buszynski and Sazlan, "Maritime Claims and Energy Cooperation," 161).

1976, April: Drilling begins at Reed Bank, and seismic surveying increases or expands to cover Amboyna (Anbo) Cay (NSQDDSJ 50-55; NSZGSZHS 35; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 20). After China protests, Philippines replies that Reed Bank is on its continental shelf, and it has no plans of stopping as of June.  In mid-June Montana Mineral Resources (蒙大拿矿物资源公司) contracts with Salan Group, and in October they announce plans to drill another well which is carried out by July 1977. A Chinese sources says the consortium drilled 5 wells by 1980 (NSQDDSJ 105-106). A subsidiary of the US Indiana Oil Company cooperated with the Philippines to drill at Reed Bank in 1978. (NSZGSZHX 371). Ultimately, the drilling found the Sampaguita Gas Field in the Reed Bank, but it was considered uncommercial and abandoned (PXP, "SC 72 Recto Bank")

1977: Philippines occupies Flat Island (Patag/费信岛) (AMTI, "Island Features"). Reportedly not occupied full-time until 2011, and controlled instead from neighbouring Nanshan/Lawak/马欢 Island (Vuving, "Who Occupies What"). This constitutes an expansion of existing Nanshan outpost.

1978 March: Philippines occupies Loaita Nan (双黄沙洲) (NSZGSZHS 121; Chen Jie PhD p.152). According to Philippines deputy defense minister, Philippines now occupies 7 features in the Spratlys (note: this number presumably includes Flat Island which was semi-occupied in 1977: Thitu, Northeast, Loaita, Nanshan, West York, Flat). Philippines then claims to have actually occupied this feature for several years. (NSQDDSJ 59-60; 62).
other_possible_cases: 1978: AMTI claims Philippines occupied Commodore Reef and Loaita Island, but this appear to be mistaken.

description: 1978 June 11: President Marcos issues Presidential Decree no. 1596 (Declaring Certain Areas Part of the Philippine Territory and Providing for their Government and Administration) and Decree 1599 (Establishing an Exclusive Economic Zone and for Other Purposes), the former incorporating Kalayaan as a municipality of Palawan province and the latter including Kalayaan within the Philippines new baselines. (Hayton, The South China Sea, 70; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 20, 59; Carranza, The Kalayaan Island Group, 53-54)

1978 Febuary: Philippines builds airstrip on Pagasa (Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao"). Other sources confirm as being constructed in the 1970s (Venzon, "Philippines set to fix airstrip on South China Sea island")
1980, January 20: First Kalayaan Mayoral election. (Luci-Atienza & Cahiles-Magkilat, "Friendly settlemenet of Pag-asa"; Municipality of Kalayaan, "Historical Background.")

1980 July 28: Philippines occupies Commodore Reef (司令礁), establishes garrison, destroys Malaysian markers, and erects Phlippine flag. (NSZGSZHS 122, 205-206; NSQDDSJ 86, 97-98; Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force, 525-526)
other_possible_cases: One Chinese source lists 1980 for when Kalayaan Island Group was incorporated in Palawan, turned into city, and Mayor appointed. (NSQDDSJ 86; 119)

description: 1981 May 8: Reported that Philippines arrested Taiwanese fishermen operating in disputed waters. (NSQDDSJ 196)
1982 April 25: Philippine officials, including the Prime Minister, inspect Zhongye Island (NSZGSZHS 122; Fravel 2008 p.290). Visits also reported in 1983, 1985, and 1986 (NSZGSZHS 122-123).
other_possible_cases: 1982, June 8: Kota (Loaita) and Panata (Lankiam) islands were designated as marine turtle sanctuaries by the Ministry of National Resources (MNR) when it issued Administrative Order No. 8. (Wikipedia "Kalayaan, Palawan")

description: 1983 January 1: Marcos issues Presidential Decree no. 1857 granting new incentives for deepwater oil exploration, revising 1972's Presidential Decree no. 87, the 'Oil Exploration and Development Act'. (Decrees available on Philippines Dept of Energy website; also see NSQDDSJ 94).

1980-1985: Philippines strengthens its defenses on occupied islands in the Spratlys. (NSQDDSJ 203) Marcos in 1982 ordered an increased presence in Spratlys. (Fravel 2008 p.290) Not entirely clear when and in what form, but there is little doubt some consolidation happened throughout the decade.

1987 December 1: Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs publishes document outling position on Kalayaan. It argues that under Spanish rule Philippine people used some of the islands as fishing bases, but the islands were uninhabited and did not belong to any country. It argues that the Cloma's activities (first 1947-1950 and 1956) are a basis for Philippine sovereignty. (NSQDDSJ 117-119; NSZGSZHS 343).
other_possible_cases: 1987 November 19: The Philippines Senate Foreign Relations Committee included the Spratly Islands as Philippine territory in a draft law (NSZGSZHS 47; NSQDDSJ 116). According to Chen Jie, sparked strong reaction from China and the bill was tabled (Chen Ji

description: 1988, January 18: Kalayaan Municipality demilitarized. A Vietnamese source states that in April the "government of the Philippines had a mayor elected as head of the municipality set up on some islets in the Truong Sa archipelago...thus conferring a more solid administrative basis on this claim to the islands." (Reference Book 'Sovereignty over the two…')
diminished_notes: 1988 August: Philippines proposes joint management (共管) to resolve the disputes. Mentions joint development (共同开发) (NSQDDSJ 166-167). Unclear if 1st time, or if this would count as diminished
other_possible_cases: 1988: The Philippines allegedly deployed troops/weapons to its islands, but the Philippine defense ministry has not confirmed. (NSQDDSJ 160)

description: 1988 May: Philippines survey ship inspects economic resources in the Spratly Islands. (NSQDDSJ 160). Repeated in 1989 (Carranza, The Kalayaan Islands Group, 50).

1989, September 4: Crestone purchases exploration rights for Philippines' GSEC 54 concession covering 1.5m hectares from offshore Palawan down towards Borneo. Then in April 1990 Crestone sells 70% stake in Philippines GSEC 54 block to BP for several million dollars. (Hayton, The South China Sea, p. 124)
other_possible_cases: 1990: Kalayaan Mayoral elections were also in 1990 (Carranza, The Kalayaan Islands, 54). However, this is covered as an ongoing behavior from 1980.

description: 1990: Shell drilling finds significant gas at Malampaya, 80km off Palawan, straddling the nine-dash line (State Department, "08MANILA2238").
1990, November: Philippines Air Force Commander tours Spratlys (Chen Jie PhD p.178). Assuming he did not visit any Malaysian-claimed features.
1990, November: Philippines military exercises in Kalayaan Group, AFP orders expansion of Thitu airstrip to allow C-130s to land (Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao").

1991, May 8: Philippines announces arrest of Taiwanese fishers. (Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ, 196). There were also two incidents that year in which Philippines briefly detained and then released Chinese fishers at Pagasa Island (PHL Memorial, Annex 21)

1992, Feb 20: Philippines military Chief of General Staff Abadia warns that Philippines will fight for its claims in the Spratlys. ('Manila Vows To Fight Over Disputed Spratly Islands'). On November 10 1992 the Philippines foreign minister says that if a war occurs in the South China Sea the US has an obligation to defend the Philippines (and later calls for clarification from the US?) (NSQDDSJ 237; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 26).
other_possible_cases: 1992 November 10 (and December?): Philippines foreign minister says that if a war occurs in the South China Sea the US has an obligation to defend the Philippines (and later calls for clarification from the US?) (NSQDDSJ 237; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands D

description: 1992, March-August: Philippines arrests of Chinese fishermen in disputed area intensify. In March, fishermen are arrested and then released after 1-2 weeks. (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 25; NSQDDSJ 217-218). On August 29, the Philippines air force commander says that the Philippines had detained another 12 Chinese fishermen (NSQDDSJ 232; Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao).

1992 July: Philippines steps up attempts to internationalize the dispute, with some success. At ASEAN Ministers Meeting, Philippines proposes an international conference on the SCS, which meets resistance, but the push is credited with helping bringing about ASEAN's Manila Declaration of 22 July. (Baviera, The Philippines and the South China Sea Dispute, 164; Buszynski and Sazlan, Maritime Claims and Energy Cooperation, 153; Hayton, The South China Sea, 192)
1992: Philippines military rebuilds Scarborough Shoal lighthouse. Manila registers it with the International Maritime Organization (Rosen, "Philippine Claims," p.12)
1993 May: Philippines president Ramos orders extension of airstrip in the Spratlys on Thitu/Pagasa/Zhongye (NSQDDSJ 247) Unclear exactly when work began.
1993, July: During 1993 ASEAN Ministers' Meeting Philippines FM Romulo makes statement, "Raising Attention on the SCS." Calls out China, talks about internationalizing the issue. (NSQDDSJ 249)
other_possible_cases: 1993 September 17: Philippines Senate Deputy proposes amendment to RP Laws 3046 and 5446 to enclose the Spratlys within the country's baselines to strengthen the Philippines' claims. (NSQDDSJ 252) Only proposed so doesn't count.

description: 1993, July-August: Philippines Navy removes PRC markers at Mischief Reef and other features (Zhang, "Appendix II," p. 3, citing Hainan Provincial Office source).

1994 January: Defence Secretary De Villa says Philippines may invoke the US defence treaty if its forces were attacked by other claimants in the Spratly islands (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 29).
other_possible_cases: 1995 February: Philippines legislature passes Armed Forces Modernization Law (Baviera, The Philippines and the South China Sea Dispute, 164). Deployments of said assets would constitute intensified assertiveness.

description: 1994 May: Philippines approves application of U.S. oil company Vaalco and Philippine subsidiary Alcorn to conduct "desktop" oil assessments of 1.5 million sq km including Reed Bank. (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 31; Storey, Creeping Assertiveness, 97; Kivimaki 56; Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao dashi nianbiao") Announced publicly on 6 July. (Dzurek, "China Occupies Mischief Reef," p. 67)
other_possible_cases: 1994 March 29: Vietnam publicly backed Philippine President Ramos’ proposal to demilitarize the Spratly islands, and agreed to carry out  joint marine research in the area. (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 29).

description: 1995 February-August: Philippines government publicizes photographic evidence of China occupying Mischief Reef and presses for further ASEAN involvement, securing an expression of "serious concern" from ASEAN Ministers in March. (Hayton, The South China Sea, 86-88, 193; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 34-35; Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force, 526; NSQDDSJ, 273-277). This has been a regular practice of the Philippines in response to assertive PRC moves since, with notable exmaples in 1998 and especially 2012 onwards..
diminished_notes: Alcorn oil investigations stall. (Dzurek, "The Spratly Islands Dispute", 39)
other_possible_cases: 1995 February: "Ramos finally approved the release of P178-million for the mapping, survey, and construction of lighthouses in the [Kayalaans]." However, were never built. (Ellen Torsedillas, 'Why the Philippines did not build lighthouses in Spratlys' | A

description: 1995, February 15: Philippines sends additional troops to the Spratlys and increases reconnaissance (Dzurek, "China Occupies Mischief Reef," p. 67)

1995 March: Philippines destroys Chinese markers on features including Jackson Atoll, Half Moon Shoal and Sabina Shoal (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 37-38; NSQDDSJ, 278; Philippines Memorial, Annex 21). Others named include First Thomas (Xinyi) and Second Thomas (Zhang, Appendix II, 5)

1995: Detentions of PRC fishers in the Spratly Islands. On March 25 the Philippine navy detains four PRC boats and 62 fishermen near Alicia Annie Reef (9°23’N, 115°27’E), and presses charges (Philippines Memorial, Annexes 19-20; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 37). June 2: "Sixty-two Chinese fishermen earlier arrested for fishing on Philippine waters refuse to recognize the court's jurisdiction during the arraignment, Wednesday [31st May], for illegal possession of explosives and poison. The fishermen from Hainan island in southern China insisted they never entered Philippine territory. Mak Yun-chui, captain of one of the four fishing boats seized by the Philippine Navy on Half Moon Shoal, said they did not enter Philippine territory and were fishing along Nansha, or the Chinese name for the Spratlys. For refusing to prove to the charges, prompted the court to enter a plea of not guilty on their behalf [as received]." (BBC Monitoring via Taffer dataset).

1995 May: Philippines naval vessel approaches Mischief Reef with 36 journalists on board, some of whom were foreign, and flew helicopters over the reef (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 37; NSQDDSJ 279-280).

1996, December: Philippines starts bolstering its capabilities in the Spratlys.  In April 1997 the Philippines deployed an additional company of marines (approximately 200 men) to the Spratlys, placed government agencies on alert,  scrambled fighter jets, made a diplomatic protest, and President Ramos made a statement, in response to the sightings of Chinese warships near Kota and Panata Islands, and the sighting of a newly built hut like structure on an unnamed reef. (MID 3.0 Narratives #4028; Taffer dataset). Also in December 1996 the Philippines lobbies unsuccessfully to get the issue onto the agenda of US-Philippines mutual defense board meetings, and follows this up by disclosing this to the media. (AFP via Taffer dataset).

1997 April: The Philippine navy strengthens on-water control around Scarborough Shoal. Navy orders a Chinese speedboat and two fishing boats to leave Scaborough Shoal; Philippine fishermen removed Chinese markers and raise their flag (Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force, 527; Storey, Creeping Assertiveness, 98). Ham radio enthusiasts also intimidated by low-flying planes and gunboats (Sherry, "Law of the Seize."). This case covers the pursuit of on-water administrative control, but not specific practices relating to  fishing rights/resources.
other_possible_cases: 1997 April: Philippines deployed an additional company of marines (approximately 200 men) to the Spratlys, placed government agencies on alert,  scrambled fighter jets, made a diplomatic protest, and President Ramos made a statement, in response to the si

description: 1997 May-July: Detaining and charging of Chinese fishers for poaching around Scarborough Shoal begins, and lasts through to at least 2000. In May Philippines arrested 21 Chinese fishermen for poaching off the Scarsborough Shoal. (MID 3.0 Narratives #4028).  In July Philippines arrested at least 23 Chinese and Hong Kong fishermen because of "illegal entry and illegal fishing." Chinese Embassy secretary said China would consider official protest. On September 23, 1997, the fishermen were released. (MID 3.0 Narratives #4028). The policy continues into 1998: On January 17 & March 11 1998: The Philippine arrests 22 and 29 Chinese fishermen respectively close to Scarborough Shoal and charges them with possession of protected marine turtles and corals (PHL Memorial, Annex 28-29; Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force, 527; Deutsche Presse-Agentur). And on November 21, 1998: PHL arrests 20 Chinese fishermen near Mischief Reef and charges them with illegal fishing. (PHL Memorial Annex 37; Storey, Creeping Assertiveness, 98).  The practice of apprehensions continued through at least 2000 (PHL Memorial, Annex 41-42).

1997 May: Philippine congresspeople Roque Ablan and Jose Yap sail to Scarborough Shoal and plant a Philippine flag for the first time since 1961. (DFA, "Background"; Storey, Creeping Assertiveness, 98). Congresspeople and reporters also visited Thitu on May 18 (Zhang, Appendix II, 7; Taffer dataset).

1997 June: Philippines blasted concrete slabs and pulled up buoys at Sabina (Xianbin) Reef in the Spratly Islands. In the same month, Philippine navy patrolmen fired warning shots at a Chinese fishing vessel near Kota Island and Spratly Islands. (Zhang, Appendix II, 7 citing The Weekend Australian; MID 3.0 Narratives #4028).
1997, June 30-July 2: Philippines' geodetic survey agency NAMRIA conducts topographic survey of Scarborough Shoal, leaves markers on its 6 protruding rocks. (Philippines Memorial, Annex 27)

1998: Manila's multilateral and internationalizing diplomacy intensifies, as Manila begins a concerted push for an official code of conduct at the Second Meeting of the Technical Working Group on Legal Matters, and pushes for international law being used in the dispute (Wiegand and Beuck, Strategic Selection, 4).

1998 August: Shell Philippines Exploration BV awarded Brown & Root a $432m design, procurement, fabrication, installation and commissioning contract for the Malampaya gas field, straddling the 9-dash line. Drilling and construction proceeded, and production began in December 2001 (Offshore Technology, "Malampaya"; Buszynski and Sazlan, Maritime Claims and Energy Cooperation, 161).

1998, August 5 the  US and Philippines stage 18-hour live-fire air and sea drills near the disputed area. On August 7 President Estrada flags "six more exercises of that kind" without stating when or where (Dow Jones & AFP via Taffer dataset). Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA) had been signed between Philippines and US in February. (Baviera, The Philippines and the South China Sea Dispute, 164; Buszynski and Sazlan, Maritime Claims and Energy Cooperation, 150).

1998, October: PRC  complains about the low-flying PHL surveillance flights around Mischief Reef (PHL Memorial Annex 34-35).  PHL reportedly also instructs its navy to fire warning shots if PRC ships come too close (Taffer dataset). PHL allegedly discontinued the flights in November (PHL Memorial Annex 36), but the PRC complained again and a March 24, 1999 report quoted a PHL official saying the flights were continuing (Taffer dataset).

1998 October: Philippine government publishes images of Chinese vessels unloading construction materials at Mischief Reef. (Storey, Creeping Assertiveness, 98). This arguably constitutes a constant line of behaviour running through to 2015, in response to major PRC provocations. Issues in play are administrative control (the PRC provocation) and political support (the PHL response).

1999 May-July: Three sinkings of PRC trawlers in as many months. In May Philippine warship sank a Chinese fishing boat in collision off Scarborough Shoal. (Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force, 527; Zhang Jie, Huangyan Island Model). In June another Chinese fishing boat sinks after a collision with a Philippine naval vessel near the Spratly Islands (PHL Memorial Annex 39; "Chinese Fishing Boat Sinks Off Disputed Spratlys," Deutsche Presse-Agentur, July 20, 1999, via Tiki toki timeline). And in July another sinking in a collision with a Philippine warship off Scarborough Shoal.” (Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force, 528).
other_possible_cases: 1999, March: Infrastructure upgrades at Thitu (Zhang, Appendix II, 8). However, this seems to be a MFA spokesperson Zhu Bangzao remark in response to a reported comment by PHL officials flagging an intention to expand the airport and build military facili

description: 1999, May 7: Occupation of Second Thomas Shoal via grounding of BRP Sierra Madre (Philippines vs. China Award, p. 438). Scarborough Shoal is also briefly occupied in the same manner but the ship was removed prior to a November visit to Manila by PRC Premier Zhu Rongji. (CND, "ASEAN Summit to face Spratly dispute"; Laude, "'Phl lost Panatag Shoal'"; Zhang, Appendix II, 8)

1999 October: “According to Philippine defense sources, two Malaysian fighter planes and two Philippine air force surveillance planes nearly engaged over a Malaysian-occupied reef in the Spratlys.” (Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force, 528; EIA, “South China Sea Backgrounder.”)

2000 February: Intensification of coercion with shots fired at Scarborough Shoal. Ambassador Fu Ying later informs Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon Jr. that Beijing would file a diplomatic protest (Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force, 528).
diminished_notes: 2000: PRC fishers arrested at Scarborough allowed to sign confession and escape with catch confiscated, rather than charges being laid. The practice of apprehensions continued (PHL Memorial, Annex 41-42).

description: 2000 May 26: Further intensification of coercive enforcement against PRC fishers/militia. “Philippine troops opened fire on Chinese fishermen in the waters off the Philippines’ island Palawan, killing one and arresting seven.” (Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force, 528; China Makes Representations to the Philippines on Killing of Fisherman,” Xinhua News Agency, June 2, 2000)

2001, Jan-March: Board-seize-eject method of fisheries enforcement expands to the Spratlys. From January through March, the Philippine navy boarded 14 Chinese-flagged boats, confiscating catches and ejecting them from Spratly area. (Van Pham, "The Use or Threat of Force," 528; AFP, "China Summons Philippine Official Over Sea Dispute"; CNN, “Row Grows Over Disputed Spratly Island."). This method continued to be used at Scarborough Shoal regularly through 2006 (PCA, "Award," 323-325).
diminished_notes: No known killings of PRC fishermen/milita; no reports of shots fired at Scarborough
other_possible_cases: 2001: First US-Philippines Balikatan exercises. Need to verify when first exercises near disputed area were, and when the first amphibious-themed exercises were.

description: 2001 March: Philippines sends a warship to Scarborough Shoal to pre-empt any PRC attempts to (re)construct sovereignty markers (Van Pham, "The Use or Threat of Force," 528; EIA, “South China Sea Backgrounder").
2001: Philippines begins transplanting civilians to Thitu in the Spratly Islands (PCA, "Award,"  193; Hayton, The South China Sea, 105; CSIS 2017, 236)

2002, Feb 10: Detentions and application of violence against PRC fishers/militia at Scarborough Shoal. PRC internal source states nine armed Philippines military police boarded Chinese fishing boats near Scarborough Shoal, order them to sign documents, detaining and beating them when they refused. On August 31 the Philippines Navy seized 14 Chinese fishers & 4 dinghies at Scarborough Shoal. China protests, Philippines claims it thought it was rescuing HK fishers missing in the Spratlys. (NISCSS 2002 report, 36-37; Taffer data). As of Sept 13, PHL was holding 122 Chinese fishers; they pleaded guity in court and were freed, but with six boats confiscated (Taffer data).
other_possible_cases: 2002: On the 104th anniversary of the founding of the Philippines Navy, Gloria Arroyo praises their detentions of Chinese fishers, in front of the Chinese ambassador (NISCSS 2002 report p.37).

description: 2002, June: Philippines awards Reed Bank service contract GSEC-101, later known as SC72, to Sterling Energy Ltd for an initial two-year term to study the prospects at Sampaguita (PXP Energy Corporation, "SC 72 Recto Bank"; Batongbacal, "Functional usage…").
other_possible_cases: 2002: Philippines boarded more than 50 Chinese fishing boats. (NISCSS 2003 report, 36-7) Basic continuity with policy since 2000.

description: 2003, April: PHL politicians attend 25th anniversary ceremony for the Kalayaan Island Group on Thitu (Zhang, Appendix II, 9).
diminished_notes: No reports of violence/detention of PRC fishermen/miltia, though boardings and confiscations continued.

description: 2003, October: Philippines’ holds “first ever transparent bidding round” for big foreign companies to conduct offshore exploration, with Energy Secretary Vicente Perez announcing the opening of 46 exploration blocks in the Malampaya as well as northwest, southeast, and east of Palawan. (Hayton, The South China Sea, 131; Buszynski and Sazlan, Maritime Claims and Energy Cooperation, 161, 163).
2003, November: PHL removes PRC markers in Spratlys (Zhang, Appendix II, 8-9). Foreign Secretary Ople later said the PRC hadn't built any "new structures or installations" in PHL areas (Taffer data).
2005, August 19: Forum Energy announces completion of seismic survey of Sampaguita prospect in Reed Bank (Taffer data).

2005, December 30: PHL Navy detains 4 Chinese fishing boats near Scarborough. A Navy report states that "The Philippine Navy maintains its position that the operation in Scarborough Shoal was a legitimate exercise of Philippine sovereignty over the area" (PHL Memorial, Annex 57-58). Although the PHL Navy implemented, "exercise of soveriegnty" suggests the issue was administrative control, not security threats.

2006, Jan 13: PHL DOE awarded SC 59 (off SW Palawan) to PNOC EC, covering an area of 14,760 km2 north of the deep-water gas discoveries in offshore Malaysia (PNOC-EC, SERVICE CONTRACT NO. 59 – WEST BALABAC).

2006, April 27: According to the PRC a Philippine fishing vessel attacked a Chinese fishing boat at Southern Bank (南方浅滩) near Reed Bank in the eastern Spratlys: four Chinese fishermen were killed and three were injured (State Council, "China Adheres"; Fisheries Administration, Zhongguo Yuye Nianjian 2007, 139 and 147). PRC accounts are very detailed and include names, so the account seems credible.
other_possible_cases: 2006, June: "the Philipppines started to renovate and upgrade the air strip and other facilities on [Thitu/Pagasa/Zhongye] island. (Fu Ying & Wu Shicun)

description: 2008 February 5: Philippines military chief visits Kalayaan. other_possible_cases: 2008 March: Possible infrastructure upgrades, but seemingly very minor. Philippines set up satellite communications facilities on some of the occupied islands and shoals, according to PRC officials. (Fu Ying & Wu Shicun). "Philippine Air Force Commander L

description: 2010, Feb 15: Forum Energy's Reed Bank licence was converted to a Service Contract. "Forum Energy immediately conducted geological and geophysical works to further evaluate the block and to fulfil its commitment to the government." (PXP Energy Corporation, "SC 72 Recto Bank")
other_possible_cases: 2010, July: MFA in Beijing summons PHL ambassador to accuse PHL marines at Second Thomas Shoal of firing a warning shot. (Jamandre, "RP faces new tensions")

description: 2010, July (approx): PRC formally protests alleged construction at Second Thomas Shoal (Jamandre, "RP faces new tensions"). other_possible_cases: 2010, late May: Nine PRC fishers detained at Half Moon Shoal, accused of hunting sea turtles (Taffer data). They were in detention for at least six days as of the report, unclear if they were charged or released.

description: 2010, late May: Nine PRC fishers detained at Half Moon Shoal, accused of hunting sea turtles (Taffer data). They were in detention for at least six days as of the report, unclear if they were charged or released.

2011, Feb-March: PHL DoE gives green light for Forum Energy to conduct seismic surveys of Reed Bank. PHL Coast Guard sends three escort ships and two surveillance planes to the area after the survey ship is harassed (Thayer, "China's New Wave", 6-7; Taffer data). "After the incident the Philippines announced a temporary halt to seismic testing and then ordered the Philippine Navy and Philippines Coast Guard to escort the survey ship when testing resumed.” (Thayer, Chinese Assertiveness, 79).
